title: Core Capabilities

course_overview.overview: This lesson introduces the core ideas behind core capabilities and prepares parents to apply the skills in real-life moments. It blends trauma-informed practice, relational safety, and practical strategies that can be used immediately[cite: 7].

learning_outcomes: Understand the purpose and value of core capabilities[cite: 7].
Identify common challenges and how to respond calmly[cite: 7].
Practice simple, repeatable strategies that build confidence[cite: 7].
Strengthen connection and emotional safety during difficult moments[cite: 7].

behavioral_guidelines: Focus on foundational executive function and regulation skills[cite: 7].
Support caregivers in modeling emotional regulation[cite: 7].

facilitator_dialogue_flow.script: Welcome. Understanding our own core capabilities is the first step toward helping our children develop theirs.

key_concepts: Why core capabilities matters for child development[cite: 7].
How trauma and stress impact behaviour[cite: 7].
How parents can model emotional regulation[cite: 7].
Predictability and routine as stabilising tools[cite: 7].
practice_activities: Try a 2-minute grounding exercise before responding to your child[cite: 7].
Practice naming emotions using simple, non-judgemental language[cite: 7].
Role-play a challenging moment and rehearse a calm script[cite: 7].
Identify one routine where core capabilities can be used daily[cite: 7].
facilitator_notes: Normalise struggle — parents often feel shame around these skills[cite: 7].
Use examples that reflect diverse families and lived experiences[cite: 7].
Pause often for reflection and emotional processing[cite: 7].
Model co-regulation through tone, pacing, and presence[cite: 7].
reflection_prompts: What part of core capabilities feels easiest for me?[cite: 7]
What part feels hardest, and why?[cite: 7]
How did my own childhood shape my reactions?[cite: 7]
What is one small change I can try this week?[cite: 7]
printable_summary:
core capabilities — Key Takeaways:
- Stay calm and predictable[cite: 7].
- Use simple language[cite: 7].
- Focus on connection before correction[cite: 7].
- Practice small steps consistently[cite: 7].
